problem: Prior embodied-perception exploration (Semantic Curiosity) builds a 2D label map that projects objects at different heights onto the same cell, so its inconsistency signal is noisy. It also ignores predicted-distribution uncertainty and labels every observation on a trajectory, wasting annotation.
motivation: Perception models pre-trained on internet images generalize poorly to new embodied scenes, and labeling is costly. An agent can move to get multi-view observations, so multi-view consistency and model uncertainty can act as self-supervised signals for choosing the most informative samples to label.
key_idea: Build a 3D semantic distribution map by EMA-fusing per-pixel class probabilities across views, use KL disagreement and top-2 class-probability uncertainty as RL curiosity rewards to explore, then label only hard (uncertain) samples on the trajectories to fine-tune the detector.
insight: Ablations show every component contributes: replacing the exploration policy with Semantic Curiosity (SC+HSS) gives 33.36 vs 34.07 AP50, and removing hard sample selection gives 33.11. Removing SDD gives 33.21 and removing SDU gives 33.59. Selecting hard samples with a threshold gives decent performance with far fewer images (9k images at δ=0.3 reaches 32.44 vs 34.07 with 20k at δ=0.1). Entropy as the uncertainty measure is slightly better (34.34) than the second-max heuristic.
method: 3D semantic distribution map: K×L×W×H voxel tensor (obstacle, explored, C class-probability channels) built from Mask R-CNN per-pixel distributions, depth and pose, fused over time by EMA (λ=0.3) as pseudo ground truth.
Disagreement reward r_d: KL(m_t, M_{t-1}) between the current view's voxel distribution and the map, rewarding objects whose distributions differ across viewpoints.
Uncertainty reward r_u: binary reward when the second-largest class probability exceeds δ (0.1), i.e. two classes are nearly tied.
Exploration policy: a CNN+FC global policy picks a long-term x-y goal every 25 steps, trained with PPO; Fast Marching Method plans the low-level actions; detector frozen.
Hard sample selection: keep images whose object second-max probability u > δ, so only images the detector finds ambiguous are labeled.
Fine-tuning and iteration: label the selected images and fine-tune Mask R-CNN (lr 0.001, Detectron2), and optionally retrain the exploration policy n times progressively with the latest model.
Real-robot deployment: run the learned policy on a Kinect V2 robot in a 60 m² house to gather 170 hard samples for fine-tuning.

setting.backbone: Mask R-CNN (FPN, ResNet-50, fine-tuned) as perception model; CNN+FC PPO exploration policy trained from scratch
setting.training_data: Mask R-CNN pre-trained on COCO restricted to 6 categories overlapping with Matterport3D; then fine-tuned on about 20k self-collected, labeled images from 54 Matterport3D train scenes; policy trained 500k steps
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + depth + 3-DOF pose (perfect pose and depth assumed)
setting.action_space: 3 discrete low-level actions (forward, left, right) with global long-term goals every 25 steps via Fast Marching Method planning
setting.privileged: perfect agent pose and depth; ground-truth labels for the selected images (annotation cost) used for fine-tuning

numbers.eval_set_note: 10 held-out Matterport3D test scenes, randomly collected samples
numbers.extra: about 20k training images, 1 exploration round, δ=0.1
exploration policy progressively trained 3 times; about 20k images

numbers.eval_set_note: 50 randomly collected validation images; 170 hard samples for fine-tuning
numbers.evidence: improve the detection and segmentation performances from 79.1% AP50 and 76.7% AP50 to 97.3% AP50 and 96.1% AP50

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark; the metric is AP50 on a Matterport3D detection/segmentation task. Table 1 gives per-class values as well as averages.
results: Fine-tuning with the method reaches 34.07 bbox AP50 (n=1) and 35.03 (n=3), against the pre-trained model's 24.23 (+10.80) and the strongest baseline, Semantic Curiosity, at 32.46. On segmentation the method gets 27.92/28.42 vs 27.06 for Semantic Curiosity. On the real robot, AP50 rises from 79.1/76.7 to 97.3/96.1.
limitations: Labeling segmentation masks is still costly; weak supervision is left for future work.
All samples are collected before fine-tuning, so the perception model is not updated during policy learning.
Depends on perfect pose and depth and on a limited set of 6 object categories; evaluated on a small set of scenes and one simulator.
